data.name: Firmin
data.gender_notes: Firmin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'firmus', meaning strong, steadfast, and firm. In Christian context, the name Firmin is associated with strength of faith and unwavering commitment to the teachings of Christ. The name Firmin carries the meaning “Firm, steadfast, strong” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Firmin usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, steadfast, strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Firmin total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Firmin holds a rich cultural heritage, especially in the Christian tradition. Named after the Latin word, Firmin signifies strength and resilience. Historically, there have been several prominent figures with this name. Saint Firmin of Béziers and Toulouse, a bishop in the late 4th and early 5th century, is a notable example. In Mozambique, there is a village named Firmin that is home to a large Christian community reflecting the long-standing influence of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Firmin is deeply spiritual and symbolizes strength of faith and unwavering commitment to the teachings of Christ. It is a reminder to stand firm in the face of adversity and lean on the power and love of God to overcome challenges. As the surname of saints and revered figures throughout history, Firmin is a name that inspires faith, hope, and courage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: As a name associated with Saint Saint Firmin of Gaul, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
